meta.purpose: QA/Automation Engineer skill tracker — interview-readiness focused

comfort_scale.1: Read about it / watched a video
comfort_scale.2: Tried it once, no real practice
comfort_scale.3: Used it in real work but gaps exist
comfort_scale.4: Comfortable, afraid of a technical test
comfort_scale.6: Could teach it / lead a team on it

items.notes: Used in real work. Gaps: POM fluency under pressure, dynamic waits, cross-browser config, framework structure from scratch.
study_path: Build a POM-based project from scratch (not a tutorial clone — pick a real site)
Practice explicit waits: WebDriverWait + expected_conditions — know the difference from implicit
Know how to handle iframes, shadow DOM, dropdowns, file uploads
Be able to explain your framework architecture out loud in an interview
Practice writing a test without an IDE for 30 min (whiteboard-style)

items.notes: Real job experience. Gaps: Desired Capabilities from scratch, handling different locator strategies under pressure.
study_path: Be able to write a desired capabilities block from memory (platform, deviceName, app, automationName)
Know all 5 locator strategies cold: accessibility id, id, xpath, class name, -android uiautomator
Know why xpath is a last resort and what you'd use instead
Practice launching a test against an Android emulator with no help

items.notes: Never used but similar to Selenium conceptually. Modern, faster, async-native. High demand in 2026 market.
study_path: Install and run 'npx playwright test' on a real site — just do it first
Understand: Playwright uses async/await natively vs Selenium's sync model
Learn auto-waiting — Playwright waits for elements to be actionable automatically
Learn page.locator() vs page.$() — know the modern API
Build one POM project in Playwright to translate your Selenium knowledge
Learn Playwright's built-in reporter and trace viewer

items.notes: Not on your list but appears heavily in job postings. JS-only, runs in browser, great DX.
study_path: Understand the core difference: Cypress runs inside the browser, Selenium/Playwright run outside
Learn cy.get(), cy.contains(), cy.intercept() for API stubbing
Build one basic test suite — Cypress docs are very beginner-friendly
Know when you'd choose Cypress vs Playwright (JS-only apps vs cross-browser needs)

items.notes: Image/AI-based testing tool. Niche but appears in some enterprise/government QA roles.
study_path: Low priority unless a target job specifically lists it
Know what it IS: image recognition-based testing, no DOM access needed
Use case: legacy apps, thick clients, platforms where DOM automation isn't possible
Free trial + official docs are the only real path here

items.notes: Years of real use but gaps: can't build a request from scratch, failed technical test on Swagger integration, weak on HTTP verb semantics.
study_path: HTTP VERB DRILL — memorize cold: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (full replace), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (delete)
Know status code families: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error — and the key ones: 200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 500
Build a request completely from scratch: URL, headers, auth (Bearer token), body (JSON)
Learn Postman Collections + environments — set a base_url variable and use it
Learn Pre-request scripts and Tests tab (pm.test, pm.expect, pm.response)
Swagger/OpenAPI: import a swagger.json into Postman — it auto-generates the collection. Practice this.
Know what a contract test is and how Postman validates response schema
Learn Newman — Postman's CLI runner for CI/CD integration

items.notes: Postman competitor with built-in mock server and OpenAPI support. Growing in market.
study_path: Low priority — if you know Postman deeply, APIdog is 80% transferable
Know it exists and what it offers over Postman: native mock server, better OpenAPI round-trip
30-min hands-on tutorial is enough to speak to it

items.notes: Appears frequently in Java-stack QA job postings. Code-based API testing library.
study_path: Learn the BDD syntax: given().header().when().get(url).then().statusCode(200)
Know how to deserialize JSON responses with Gson or Jackson
Medium priority if targeting Java shops — skip if Python-focused

items.notes: Know how to use tools but gaps in terminology, contract testing, auth flows.
study_path: Know these cold: endpoint, payload, headers, auth (Basic, Bearer, OAuth2, API Key)
Understand REST vs SOAP — know why SOAP is legacy and what WSDL is
Contract testing: the idea that the API response matches an agreed schema (Pact framework)
Idempotency: GET/PUT/DELETE are idempotent, POST is not — know why this matters
Mock servers: when and why you'd stub an API during testing
Know what a 422 Unprocessable Entity means vs 400 Bad Request

items.notes: Basic workflow known. Gaps: branching strategy, rebase vs merge, resolving conflicts, PR workflow.
study_path: Know these cold: clone, add, commit, push, pull, branch, checkout, merge, status, log
Understand git rebase vs git merge — when you'd use each
Practice resolving a merge conflict manually
Know Gitflow or trunk-based development at a conceptual level
Be able to explain what a PR is and how you'd do a code review

items.notes: High demand in 2026 market. YAML-based CI pipelines triggered by push/PR events.
study_path: Understand the structure: workflow > job > step
Write a basic .github/workflows/test.yml that runs your Selenium or Playwright tests on push
Know: on: push/pull_request, runs-on: ubuntu-latest, uses: actions/checkout@v3
Learn how to set secrets in GitHub and reference them in workflows
Know what an artifact is in the GitHub Actions context (uploaded test reports)

items.notes: Older but still very common in enterprise. Appears in many job postings.
study_path: Understand: Jenkins is a self-hosted CI server, GitHub Actions is cloud-native
Know what a Jenkinsfile is and basic declarative pipeline syntax
Learn pipeline > agent > stages > stage > steps structure
Medium priority — GitHub Actions knowledge transfers conceptually

items.notes: Appears in many senior QA postings. Running tests in containers is common.
study_path: Know what a container is vs a VM — elevator pitch version
Learn: docker run, docker build, docker ps, docker exec
Understand a basic Dockerfile for a Python or Node test project
Know why you'd run Selenium tests in Docker (consistent environment, parallelism)
Selenium Grid in Docker is a bonus talking point

items.notes: Know basic navigation. Gaps in writing scripts, conditionals, loops.
study_path: Know these cold: ls, cd, pwd, mkdir, rm, cp, mv, cat, grep, echo, chmod
Write a basic script: shebang line, variables, if/else, for loop
Know how to make a script executable: chmod +x script.sh && ./script.sh
Learn how to pipe commands: grep 'ERROR' test.log | sort | uniq -c
Know exit codes: 0 = success, non-zero = failure — relevant for CI

items.notes: Common in every QA role. Know the basics — deepen on test cycle vocabulary.
study_path: Know the ticket lifecycle: Backlog > In Progress > In Review > Done
Understand epics, stories, sub-tasks, and bugs as issue types
Know how to write a proper bug report: steps to reproduce, expected vs actual, environment, severity
Learn Zephyr or Xray plugin concepts — test case management within JIRA

items.notes: Strong from experience. Just needs sharper vocabulary for interviews.
study_path: Know these terms cold: smoke, sanity, regression, integration, E2E, exploratory, UAT
Test pyramid: unit (lots) > integration (some) > E2E (few) — know why
Equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis — be able to give an example
Know what risk-based testing is and when you'd apply it
Be able to answer: 'How would you test a login page?' with a structured, thorough answer

items.notes: Appears often in Java-stack job postings as the test runner under Selenium.
study_path: Know the annotations: @Test, @BeforeMethod, @AfterMethod, @BeforeClass, @DataProvider
Understand how TestNG.xml controls test execution
Medium priority — if targeting Python, know pytest instead

items.notes: Python test runner — critical if your automation portfolio is Python-based.
study_path: Know fixtures: @pytest.fixture, scope levels (function/class/session)
Know how to parametrize tests: @pytest.mark.parametrize
Know how to run: pytest -v, pytest -k 'test_login', pytest --html=report.html
Integrate with Selenium and understand conftest.py

items.notes: Self-teaching. Most common language for QA automation in 2026 market alongside Java.
study_path: Be able to write a class, method, constructor (__init__) from scratch
Know list comprehensions, dicts, and how to read/write JSON
Understand try/except for error handling in test scripts
Be comfortable with pip, virtual environments, requirements.txt
POM pattern in Python: understand how to structure Page classes

items.notes: Listed on your stack. Gaps likely in JOINs, subqueries, aggregation under interview pressure.
study_path: Know cold: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, JOIN (INNER/LEFT/RIGHT), GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
Practice writing a JOIN between two tables by hand
Know the difference between WHERE and HAVING
Know COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN
Be able to answer: 'Write a query to find all users who placed more than 3 orders'

items.notes: Needed for Playwright (TypeScript/JS) and Cypress. Not required but high demand.
study_path: Understand async/await — critical for Playwright
Know arrow functions, template literals, destructuring
Understand npm, package.json, node_modules basics
Medium priority — Python focus first, but JS opens Playwright/Cypress doors

items.notes: Progressive JS framework. Nuxt is Vue equivalent of Next.js. Worth knowing exists.
study_path: Vue is a JS frontend framework — like React but with a different syntax
Nuxt is to Vue what Next.js is to React: SSR, file-based routing, etc.
Low priority for QA automation — relevant if your team uses it and you need component tests
Vue Test Utils is the testing library — analogous to React Testing Library
Know it exists and what problems it solves

items.notes: Load/performance testing tools. Appears in senior QA and DevOps-adjacent roles.
study_path: Low priority for entry/mid-level. Know what they are and why they're used.
k6 is the modern choice — JS-based, CI-friendly
Be able to answer: 'What is load testing vs stress testing vs spike testing?'

items.notes: Open-source Firebase alternative. Postgres + auth + storage + realtime, hosted.
study_path: What it IS: a hosted Postgres database with a REST API auto-generated from your schema
Free tier is generous — good for portfolio projects
Supabase vs Railway: Supabase = managed Postgres with built-in auth/API. Railway = general app hosting.
Supabase client: npm install @supabase/supabase-js — then supabase.from(table).select()
Auth is built-in: email/password, OAuth — no need to build your own login system

items.notes: File-based DB. Used in your FastAPI portfolio projects already.
study_path: Know when to use SQLite vs Postgres: SQLite = single file, local/dev only. Postgres = production, multi-user.
Python: import sqlite3 — connect, cursor, execute, fetchall, commit
Know how to inspect a .db file: DB Browser for SQLite (GUI tool, free)
In FastAPI context: SQLAlchemy ORM vs raw sqlite3 — know the tradeoff
